answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable: the in-flight build is a compliance-mandated security patch. Circuit breaking would fail fast and drop settlement writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective, so that path is rejected despite prior partner-outage success. There is no regional fault signal, and failover of a write-heavy settlement peak would risk in-flight customer writes. The live picture is write-path p99 at 5x under daily settlement load; inherited memory_b3 is the closest match (headroom absorbing a write surge) but it describes pre-peak provisioning, so it is the single record worth verifying and the transfer to a mid-peak add is uncertain. Adding capacity is the only remaining lever that can relieve write latency without discarding customer writes. Scale is a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout because the regression could still be patch overhead rather than raw shortage, and this is the only intervention window.
